newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolian ex-communists claim local poll victory.
newsitem.headline: Mongolian ex-communists claim local poll victory.

text.p: Mongolia's former communist party, still stinging from a crushing defeat in national polls earlier this year, was on Tuesday claiming a decisive victory in the north Asian nation's local elections.

The Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP) was expecting to win about 65 percent of the vote in last Sunday's elections for the local people's hurals, or parliaments, said party secretary Enkhbayar.

The formerly communist MPRP, which lost its 76-year-old grip on Mongolia's national parliament, the Great Hural, in polls last June, would gain majorities in 15 of 21 provincial hurals, Enkhbayar told a news briefing.
Mongolians, about half of whom are nomadic herders, voted for more than 7,000 seats in provincial, county and district-level hurals in Sunday's ballot.

The General Election Committee will not announce final ballot results until October 10 because of transportation problems in the vast land of steppes, where many voters ride on horseback for miles to cast their ballots.
Local media said an MPRP victory in the provinces would give the party leverage against the central government, now dominated by the reformist Democratic Union Coalition.

In Sunday's polls, the MPRP tried to capitalise on their traditional rural electorate and tap discontent sparked by some unpopular measures of the new government such as the freeing of fuel and electricity prices in September.
The democrats have called for faster free-market reforms to help lift Mongolia out of an economic depression caused in part by the withdrawal of Soviet backing in 1991.
Voter turnout in the local ballot was 64.2 percent, far lower than in the national poll when turnout was more than 92 percent, local reports said.
